newsitem.title: UK: Car shuttle resumes in Channel tunnel after fire.
newsitem.headline: Car shuttle resumes in Channel tunnel after fire.

text.p: Passenger car service resumed through the Anglo-French Channel tunnel on Tuesday, three weeks after a fire closed down the link.
The first Le Shuttle train, carrying 61 vehicles, left the Coquelles terminal near Calais at 0630 GMT and arrived at the Cheriton terminal in England 50 minutes later.
The crossing took about 15 minutes longer than before the accident due to damage in the tunnel.
The tunnel was closed to all traffic on November 18, when a fire on a truck destroyed a freight shuttle train and severely damaged a section of the tunnel, injuring 34 people.
Rail service for passengers between Paris and London and Brussels and London resumed last Wednesday using one of the two parallel rail tunnels. The other one is still closed for repairs.
